title: 2027-01-26 Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Sierra AI
next_steps: Redwood to send revised reserved-capacity quote with APAC region add-on
Customer to share expected qps/traffic profile for next 12 months
Schedule 1-day throughput + latency benchmark on customer's test dataset (Redwood SE + Sierra infra)
Share SOC2 + network architecture docs and KMS/HSM integration guide
action_items: Lena: prepare updated pricing and contract language for 12-month extension by 2027-02-02
Amit: run capacity estimate and recommended GPU mix, deliver by 2027-01-29
Maya: send historical traffic spikes and expected seasonal peaks by 2027-01-28
Priya: provide VPC peering contacts and firewall rules doc by 2027-02-03
summary: Check-in focused on renewal timing and expansion: Sierra AI is evaluating a 12-month renewal with a dedicated capacity increase and an APAC region add-on. Main asks: expected throughput, RU/latency targets, security docs for procurement, and an on-prem-like VPC peering test. Agreement to run a 1-day benchmark and Redwood to send revised quote and contract amendments.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Morales (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time today. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya Chen (Sierra AI): Maya here.
[00:10] Jon Rivera (Sierra AI): Jon.
[00:12] Priya Singh (Sierra AI): Priya.
[00:14] Ethan Lowe (Sierra AI, Procurement): Ethan.
[00:16] Amit Patel (Redwood SE): Amit here.
[00:18] Sofia Cruz (Redwood CSM): Sofia on the line.
[00:22] Lena: Perfect. We put together a short agenda: renewal timeline, capacity needs, APAC region add, security/procurement asks, and next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Jon: Yep, that's right. We're a few months out from contract end and want to lock in runway — also need to add capacity for a new customer pilot in APAC.
[00:38] Maya: Quick context — production usage right now is ~220 qps peak for our realtime assistant, with sustained 80 qps. We expect a new launch that could double peak for a 6-8 week trial.
[00:48] Amit: Got it. When you say double, is that across same seq lengths? Are you expecting longer prompts for the pilot?
[00:55] Maya: A bit longer on average, probably 1.5x token length since we’ll include more context and retrieval outputs.
[01:02] Amit: Ok that changes the latency/throughput footprint. We'll run a capacity estimate for that profile.
[01:08] Priya: On networking — we need VPC peering and SAML SSO in place for procurement sign-off. Also KMS for key control, we prefer HSM-backed keys.
[01:17] Sofia: We have KMS/HSM integration docs and SAML guides, will share. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS but note in some cases we offer HSM guidance for Private installs.
[01:27] Ethan: From procurement — SOC2 plus data residency commitments for APAC are key. We'll need contract language for 12-month extension and termination clauses around capacity changes.
[01:36] Lena: Understood. On the renewal length, are you leaning 12 months or something else?
[01:40] Jon: 12 months makes sense if we can add APAC and the dedicated pool upgrade at a fixed commit rate.
[01:45] Lena: Great. For the dedicated capacity, what we typically do is size the reserved GPU pool — e.g., add an extra 8x A100-equivalent slots or choose a mixed quantized profile. We'll propose both a high-throughput and a cost-optimized configuration.
[01:59] Maya: We ran a PoC with Redwood last quarter but that was on shared hosted. We liked the latency, but need predictable throughput for the pilot.
[02:07] Amit: Right — dedicated lets you get predictable KPI; we also provide autoscale bursts and fallback to hosted in case of sudden spikes if you want that safety net.
[02:15] Jon: How does the APAC region add work operationally? Data residency and latency-wise?
[02:20] Amit: There are a couple of options: 1) provision a dedicated pool in APAC under the same Dedicated contract, 2) use a regional hosted endpoint (faster to stand up but less isolation), or 3) a Private deploy if you need air-gapped infra. Each has tradeoffs on cost and SLO.
[02:36] Priya: We prefer option 1 if the cost delta isn't too big — we want the isolation and consistent latencies.
[02:42] Lena: We'll include an APAC dedicated pool option in the quote. We'll call out the incremental monthly commit and a cross-region data egress note.
[02:50] Maya: Also, on model variants — we want the ability to fail over to a lower-cost quantized model if latency or cost spikes. Is that feasible?
[02:58] Amit: Yes, we support model variants and automated routing policies — can route by latency target, cost thresholds, or region. There's a small quality delta with heavy quantization, but we can include an eval set to determine acceptable regressions.
[03:12] Jon: Nice. For the benchmark, we'd like Redwood SE to run tests using our test harness against a mirrored dataset — can you do a one-day benchmark with both regions?
[03:20] Amit: Absolutely. We'll need test credentials and the qps profile. We'll coordinate to provision temporary capacity and run both latency p95 and sustained throughput tests. Expect a short pre-check and then a 6–8 hour run, but we can stretch to a day if you prefer.
[03:35] Maya: We can provide the harness and a sandbox dataset. We'll also throw in a couple of worst-case long prompts.
[03:41] Amit: Perfect. I'll prepare the runbook.
[03:44] Ethan: Procurement question — on pricing: if we increase reserved capacity and add a region, can we get a stepped discount? Also need to see termination protections if the pilot doesn't convert.
[03:54] Lena: We can tier pricing by commit level. For pilots we sometimes do a 3-month add-on that converts into the annual commit if you choose to continue; otherwise there's a defined wind-down. We'll put two contract options in the quote: a straight 12-month commit and a pilot-to-commit path.
[04:10] Priya: On SSO, we use Okta. Need SAML metadata exchange and tests. We also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[04:19] Sofia: Redwood can deliver SAML integration guide and we've sent SIEM log formats before; we'll include options for log forwarding and retention SLAs in the security packet.
[04:29] Jon: Any blockers on the Private deployment path? We might consider a private control plane for very sensitive flows.
[04:35] Amit: Private is possible but adds setup time and ops overhead. If you need air-gapped or on-prem, that typically takes longer and has a different pricing model. For most customers the APAC dedicated pool hits the sweet spot.
[04:47] Maya: Timeline — procurement wants to lock in terms by mid-February to hit Q2 roadmap.
[04:53] Lena: That's doable. We'll aim to deliver updated quote and contract language this week so legal can review.
[04:58] Amit: I'll run the capacity sizing and send recommended GPU mix — should have preliminary numbers by Friday.
[05:04] Maya: Great. A note — during our last PoC, some model names were mis-transcribed in the logs, so when you send docs call out the exact model tags and versioning.
[05:12] Amit: Good call; we'll include canonical model tags and recommended quantization profiles (e.g., q4f16) and note any perf/quality tradeoffs.
[05:21] Ethan: Contractually we need SOC2 Type II attestation and proof of encryption for data at rest and in transit — KMS/HSM details.
[05:29] Sofia: We'll attach SOC2 compliance report and an architecture diagram. For KMS, we support CMKs via AWS KMS and also HSM keywrap flows; we'll include the integration guide.
[05:39] Priya: For the bench, can we test with a prefix/KV cache warm vs cold? That's where we saw some variance last time.
[05:46] Amit: Yes, we'll include cold vs warm cache runs and show p50/p95/p99. We'll also demonstrate the prefix caching behavior; note sometimes transcript automation says KV "cash" but it's KV cache, so we will be explicit.
[05:58] Jon: Good — also want a short write-up on expected cost per 1M tokens at the various configs.
[06:05] Lena: We'll include estimated unit economics, both hosted and dedicated scenarios, and the impact of batching and caching.
[06:12] Maya: Anything else?
[06:14] Jon: No, that's it.
[06:16] Lena: OK recap: Redwood delivers updated quote with APAC and pilot path, Amit to deliver capacity estimate, Sierra provides qps and test harness, schedule benchmark (tentative next week), Redwood shares SOC2/security/KMS docs and SAML guide.
[06:30] Ethan: Sounds good. We'll review and loop in legal once we have the draft.
[06:35] Lena: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with dates and files.
[06:38] Maya: Thanks all.
[06:40] End of recording.

Notes: occasional auto-transcript typos observed (Redwood Dedicate, KV cash, etc.) — speaker labels mostly accurate but a couple of short cross-talks.
notes: Call included AE+SE+CSM from Redwood; typical procurement/security asks (SOC2, SAML, KMS/HSM). Agreed benchmark and quote delivery timeline.
